A ` ```git-sandbox-vscode ` block is a git-sandbox exercise drawn in the
real VS Code: explorer, editors and diffs, search, the Source Control view
and the integrated terminal. It takes every option a ` ```git-sandbox `
block takes, so tasks tick, **Undo** and **Reset** work, and the panels
below follow along. Each click in Source Control runs the git command it
stands for, which you can find in VS Code's **Git** output.

VS Code is a few megabytes. It is fetched when the first exercise below
scrolls into view, and stays with whichever one you scrolled to last. The
button beside **Undo** lets it fill the window. Back to the
[git-sandbox guide](example.html).

## Install

```bash
quarto add jansim/quarto-git-sandbox
```

installs both extensions. List both filters, in either order:

```yaml
filters:
  - git-sandbox
  - git-sandbox-vscode
```

## Stage and commit with Source Control

```git-sandbox-vscode
id: vscode-flow
title: The edit, stage, commit loop, in VS Code
prompt: "~/sales-analysis $"
intro: |
  {w}VS Code's terminal runs this exercise's shell.{/}
  Try the Source Control view on the left: it runs the same commands for you.
done-note: Every click in Source Control was a git command. **Show Git Output** in its **...** menu lists them.
seed: |
  git init
  echo "# Sales analysis" > README.md
  git add .
  git commit -m "Add the project README"
  echo "sales <- read_csv('sales.csv')" > load.R
tasks:
  - text: In Source Control, stage `load.R` with its **+** button
    when: staged
  - text: Write a message in the box above the changes and commit with **Ctrl+Enter**
    when: commits >= 2
  - text: Open `README.md` in the explorer, add a line, save, and find the change in Source Control
    when: commits >= 2 and not clean
```

````markdown
```git-sandbox-vscode
title: The edit, stage, commit loop, in VS Code
prompt: "~/sales-analysis $"
seed: |
  git init
  echo "# Sales analysis" > README.md
  git add .
  git commit -m "Add the project README"
  echo "sales <- read_csv('sales.csv')" > load.R
tasks:
  - text: In Source Control, stage `load.R` with its **+** button
    when: staged
```
````

## Resolve a conflict in VS Code

VS Code lists the conflicted file under **Merge Changes**, and its
terminal prompt shows `(main|MERGING)`. Fix the file in the editor, save,
stage it, and commit: the message box already holds git's merge message.

```git-sandbox-vscode
id: vscode-conflict
title: A merge conflict, in VS Code
prompt: "~/sales-analysis $"
intro: |
  Type {y}git merge title{/} below, then resolve the conflict in the editor.
seed: |
  git init
  echo "# Sales analysis" > README.md
  git add .
  git commit -m "Add the project README"
  git checkout -b title
  echo "# Sales analysis 2026" > README.md
  git commit -am "Retitle for the new year"
  git checkout main
  echo "# Quarterly sales analysis" > README.md
  git commit -am "Say which sales"
tasks:
  - text: Merge `title` into `main` and open `README.md` from **Merge Changes**
    when: conflicts
  - text: Keep the line you want, save, and stage the file
    when: merging and not conflicts and not file README.md contains "<<<<<<<"
  - text: Commit the merge
    when: merged title into main and merge commit
```

## A box, and the same repository in VS Code

`share: <id>` works here too: this exercise is VS Code on the repository
of the box above it. Work in either; the other keeps up.

```git-sandbox
id: plain-box
title: A plain box
prompt: "~/sales-analysis $"
seed: |
  git init
  echo "# Sales analysis" > README.md
  git add .
  git commit -m "Add the project README"
tasks:
  - text: Create a branch called `report` in either view
    when: branch report
```

```git-sandbox-vscode
id: plain-box-vscode
share: plain-box
title: The box above, in VS Code
tasks:
  - text: Switch to `report` from the branch name in VS Code's status bar
    when: on report
```

````markdown
```git-sandbox-vscode
share: plain-box
title: The box above, in VS Code
```
````
